items.title: Docetaxel and SX-682 Trial for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1/2 trial testing SX-682 (a new drug) combined with docetaxel chemotherapy in patients with metastatic prostate cancer that has returned after treatment or spread. The trial is not yet recruiting but offers a potential treatment option combining a novel agent with standard chemotherapy. Participants take SX-682 as a daily pill along with docetaxel infusions.

items.title: Pembrolizumab Combination Therapies for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1/2 trial evaluating pembrolizumab (an immunotherapy) combined with various standard treatments including olaparib, docetaxel, enzalutamide, abiraterone, and others for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study has multiple treatment arms testing different combinations. The trial is active but not currently recruiting new participants.

items.title: HLD-0915 Study in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1/2 trial testing HLD-0915, a new investigational drug, in patients with metastatic prostate cancer who have already received prior treatments. The study is currently recruiting patients and will assess both safety and effectiveness of this novel agent in advanced disease settings.

items.title: BNT324 versus Docetaxel Phase 3 Trial in mCRPC
items.summary: A Phase 3 trial comparing BNT324 (a new experimental drug) to standard chemotherapy (docetaxel) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who have received androgen receptor inhibitors but no prior chemotherapy. The study aims to determine if BNT324 can help patients live longer without cancer progression and improve overall survival. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: STEAP1 CAR-T Cell Therapy with Enzalutamide for mCRPC
items.summary: A Phase 1/2 trial testing CAR-T cell therapy targeting STEAP1 protein combined with enzalutamide for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. This represents a novel immunotherapy approach using genetically modified T cells to attack prostate cancer cells. The trial is currently recruiting and represents an emerging treatment strategy for advanced disease.

items.title: FTT PET/CT Imaging for PARP Activity in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A study using FTT PET/CT scans to measure PARP enzyme activity in metastatic prostate cancer before and after starting treatment. Up to 30 men will receive imaging scans and results will be compared to tissue biopsies. This research aims to develop better methods for tracking cancer and treatment response.

items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Androgen Receptor Inhibitors in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1 trial testing xaluritamig (an experimental immunotherapy) combined with either darolutamide or abiraterone in patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study is evaluating safety and tolerability of these combination approaches. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: BMS-986365 Phase 3 Trial in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 3 trial comparing BMS-986365 (an investigational drug) to physician's choice of standard therapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. This large-scale trial will evaluate whether the new drug improves outcomes compared to current treatment options. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Xaluritamig Safety Study in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1 trial determining the safety profile of xaluritamig in adults with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. This early-phase study is evaluating the investigational immunotherapy agent at the proposed treatment regimen. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide Plus Lutetium-177 PSMA in mCRPC
items.summary: A Phase 2 trial testing luxdegalutamide (JSB462) at two different doses combined with Lutetium-177 PSMA radioligand therapy compared to Lutetium-177 alone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients previously treated with androgen receptor inhibitors. The study aims to select the best combination dose for future Phase 3 trials. Not currently recruiting.

items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone Phase 3 Trial in Chemotherapy-Naïve mCRPC
items.summary: A Phase 3 trial comparing xaluritamig plus abiraterone to physician's choice (docetaxel, cabazitaxel, or abiraterone) in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have not yet received chemotherapy. The primary goal is to compare overall survival between treatment approaches. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: REGN5678 Plus Cemiplimab for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1/2 trial testing REGN5678 (nezastomig) alone or combined with cemiplimab immunotherapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study has dose escalation and expansion phases to determine safe doses and evaluate tumor shrinkage. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Lutetium-177 Dotatate for Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 2 trial studying Lutetium-177 dotatate, a radioactive drug that targets somatostatin receptors, in metastatic prostate cancer with neuroendocrine features. The treatment binds to specific proteins on neuroendocrine tumor cells and delivers targeted radiation. Currently recruiting patients with this aggressive prostate cancer variant.

items.title: Tinengotinib with Standard Treatments for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1/2 trial testing tinengotinib (TT-00420) combined with either abiraterone plus prednisone or enzalutamide in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study evaluates safety and side effects of these combination approaches. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: DNA Vaccines Plus Pembrolizumab for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 2 trial comparing one DNA vaccine (pTVG-HP) versus two DNA vaccines (pTVG-HP and pTVG-AR) given with pembrolizumab immunotherapy for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Treatment continues for up to 2 years. The study tests whether two vaccines create stronger immune responses against tumors than one vaccine. Not currently recruiting.

items.title: Radium-223 Plus M3814 Plus Avelumab for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1/2 trial comparing radium-223 radioactive treatment alone, radium-223 plus M3814 (a radiation enhancer), or all three drugs including avelumab immunotherapy for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is currently suspended but aims to find the best combination approach.

items.title: Inflammation and Epigenetic Changes Drive Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research review explains how chronic inflammation drives prostate cancer progression and treatment resistance. NFκB and IL6/JAK/STAT3 inflammatory pathways interact with androgen receptor signaling and cause epigenetic changes that help tumors survive, grow, spread, and evade the immune system. Understanding these mechanisms may lead to new treatment approaches targeting inflammation.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Boosts Anti-Tumor Immunity in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A preclinical study showing that a nanoplasmid DNA vaccine targeting PSMA (a protein overexpressed in aggressive prostate cancer) generates strong immune responses and prevents tumor growth and lung metastasis in animal models. The vaccine also enhances response to PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy and reduces immunosuppressive regulatory T cells.

items.title: PI3K/AKT Pathway Targeting in PTEN-Deficient Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A review discussing how PTEN gene loss activates the PI3K/AKT pathway in prostate cancer, driving tumor growth and treatment resistance. The article examines using biomarkers like PTEN deficiency to guide selection of PI3K/AKT pathway inhibitors for personalized treatment approaches.

items.title: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in mCRPC: Meta-Analysis Shows Limited Benefit
items.summary: A meta-analysis of 21 trials involving 1,580 metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients found that immune checkpoint inhibitors showed modest results when used alone or in dual combinations. Combination therapy with other agents showed better survival and progression-free survival benefits than immunotherapy alone, suggesting immunotherapy needs to be combined with other treatments for effectiveness.

items.title: Targeting Regulatory T Cells in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A review examining how regulatory T cells (Tregs) in the prostate tumor microenvironment help cancer evade the immune system. High Treg density in tumor stroma doubles the risk of cancer recurrence. Highly suppressive Treg subtypes are found in aggressive, high-Gleason score tumors. The review discusses current and emerging therapies targeting Tregs.

items.title: Zoledronic Acid Prevents Bone Loss from Enzalutamide Plus ADT
items.summary: The BonEnza trial showed that metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients receiving androgen deprivation therapy plus enzalutamide experience significant bone mineral density loss after 18 months. Adding zoledronic acid (a bone-strengthening medication) prevented this bone loss at both the femoral neck and lumbar spine, maintaining bone health during treatment.
